title: Master Class | Alekhine Defense | Chess Speedrun | Grandmaster Naroditsky

moves.spoken: We answer the king's pawn with the knight to f6 — the Alekhine, a rare but sound choice.
White chases with e5 and our knight hops to d5.
We retreat the knight to b6.
White plays d4, taking the centre in a measured way.
White captures on d6 — one of the two main lines.

We recapture with the c-pawn on d6 — my recommendation for Alekhine beginners, because it teaches you to handle an imbalanced structure: White gets a queenside pawn majority, we get a kingside majority.
White develops the knight to c3. Our light-squared bishop will struggle to get out, so we'll fianchetto.
We play g6, preparing the fianchetto.

We continue naturally with the knight to c6, and the plan writes itself: press White's two central pawns. It resembles a Dragon but far calmer — both sides castle short and nobody's getting mated soon. It's hard to play at club level for two reasons: you're a touch cramped, so accuracy matters, and you must know how to meet a wide range of White setups.
